First, I remember that Ronald Reagan was the President of the United States, serving from 1981 to 1989. Before that, he was the Governor of California, but that's a state position, not a federal one. So, his main federal position before the presidency was... Hmm, wasn't he the Vice President? I think he served as Vice President under President Jimmy Carter from 1977 to 1981.

Now, George H. W. Bush, who is the father of the current President George W. Bush, was also a President, serving from 1989 to 1993. Before that, I believe he was the Vice President as well, but I'm not entirely sure when. Was it during Reagan's presidency? I think so, yes. So, George H. W. Bush was Vice President from 1981 to 1989, the same time Reagan was President.

So, both Reagan and Bush held the position of Vice President of the United States. That makes sense because typically, Vice Presidents serve under the President. So, both of them were Vice Presidents before becoming President themselves.

Also, both were involved in significant political movements or events during their tenures.

Another thing I can think about is their political parties. Reagan was a Republican, and so was Bush. It's common for Vice Presidents to be from the same party as the President, especially in the U.S. system. So, both being Vice Presidents under Republican Presidents makes sense.

I don't recall any information that suggests they held a different position together. They didn't both serve as Senators or Governors at the same time, as far as I know. Their paths to the presidency were through the Vice Presidency, which is a common stepping stone.

So, putting it all together, it seems clear that both Ronald Reagan and George H. W. Bush held the position of Vice President of the United States. Reagan was Vice President before becoming President, and Bush followed a similar trajectory. Therefore, the correct answer should be that both served as Vice Presidents.
